purpose: Establish the stock Galaxy A35's Cell Broadcast surface using read-only inspection only.

safety.rationale: Every command below reads state. None writes a setting, installs anything, clears data, remounts a partition, or touches a user file. If any command in this batch produces output that looks like a state change, stop and report it as a defect in this batch rather than continuing.
not_included_on_purpose: am start / am broadcast of any test component (attempts delivery; deferred to a later batch that needs explicit approval)
su, root, magisk, bootloader or fastboot operations

setup: On the phone: Settings > About phone > tap Build number 7 times to enable Developer options.
Settings > Developer options > enable USB debugging.
Connect by USB. On the phone accept the 'Allow USB debugging?' prompt.
On the laptop, confirm exactly one device is listed and authorized: adb devices -l
If it says 'unauthorized', unlock the phone and accept the prompt, then re-run adb devices -l.

how_to_return_evidence.body: the raw stdout of the command, verbatim, unedited
how_to_return_evidence.rule: Send raw output. Do not summarise, and do not add a conclusion about whether an alert appeared. Any interpretation is done on the receiving side from the raw text.
how_to_return_evidence.powershell_example: $o = adb shell getprop ro.build.version.release; Invoke-WebRequest -Method Post -Uri "$base/evidence" -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $token"; 'X-Evidence-Name' = 'a35-01-identity.txt' } -Body ([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($o))

evidence_name_convention: a35-NN-topic.txt, zero-padded, matching the number of each task

tasks.title: Device identity and build
tasks.reason: Which Android version and which build type. This determines whether we are looking at a retail user build at all, and gives us the exact model string for the record.

tasks.title: Security and integrity state
tasks.reason: Confirms the phone is genuinely stock and unmodified, and records it so the claim 'stock' is evidence-backed rather than assumed. Also shows us the constraints we are working inside.

tasks.title: Which Cell Broadcast packages exist
tasks.reason: The single most important question in Phase 4: what owns alerts on this phone. AOSP ships com.android.cellbroadcastreceiver; Samsung may ship its own alongside or instead. -u includes packages that are installed but disabled, which would otherwise be invisible.
commands: adb shell pm list packages | Select-String -Pattern cellbroadcast
adb shell pm list packages -u | Select-String -Pattern cellbroadcast
adb shell pm list packages | Select-String -Pattern emergency
adb shell pm list packages | Select-String -Pattern 'wsa|wirelessalert'
adb shell pm list packages | Select-String -Pattern com.samsung.android.cellbroadcast
adb shell pm list packages | Select-String -Pattern com.android.cellbroadcast

tasks.title: Receiver package: components, permissions, signature
tasks.reason: The heart of the security-boundary question. dumpsys package shows every declared receiver and service, whether each is exported, the permissions that protect them, and the protection level and owning UID of those permissions. This is what lets us say precisely why an external trigger is or is not possible, rather than guessing.
tasks.note: Long output. Send it whole and unedited; do not trim. If the package name does not exist on this device, that is itself the finding.

tasks.title: Whether Cell Broadcast ships as an APEX on this build
tasks.reason: On recent Android the module is an updatable APEX, which changes where the code lives and which version is running. It also tells us whether Samsung has overridden the module.
commands: adb shell pm list packages | Select-String -Pattern apex

tasks.title: Emergency-alert permissions and their protection levels
tasks.reason: Establishes whether the permission that guards the emergency broadcast is signature|privileged. If it is, an ordinary app can never hold it, and that is the security boundary stated with evidence instead of assumption.
commands: adb shell dumpsys package | Select-String -Pattern RECEIVE_EMERGENCY_BROADCAST
adb shell dumpsys package | Select-String -Pattern SEND_EMERGENCY_BROADCAST
adb shell dumpsys package | Select-String -Pattern READ_CELL_BROADCASTS
adb shell dumpsys package | Select-String -Pattern RECEIVE_SMS
adb shell pm list permissions -g -f | Select-String -Pattern emergency -Context 3

tasks.title: Live Cell Broadcast service and telephony state
tasks.reason: Confirms the service is running and shows the channel configuration the phone is actually using. Also records the real carrier, which matters for the network-side question in Phase 5.
commands: adb shell dumpsys activity services | Select-String -Pattern cellbroadcast -Context 6
adb shell dumpsys activity services | Select-String -Pattern CellBroadcastService -Context 6
adb shell dumpsys carrier_config | Select-String -Pattern broadcast -Context 2,6
adb shell dumpsys telephony.registry | Select-String -Pattern broadcast
tasks.note: On Samsung, dumpsys carrier_config may require a filter; if it errors, send the error verbatim.

tasks.title: Current emergency-alert user settings
tasks.reason: Alerts can be enabled or disabled per category by the user, and the AOSP research established that a preference gate can make a delivered message invisible. We need the phone's actual settings before drawing any conclusion from an absent alert.
commands: adb shell settings list global | Select-String -Pattern 'emergency|cell_broadcast|cellbroadcast'
adb shell settings list secure | Select-String -Pattern 'emergency|cell_broadcast|cellbroadcast'
adb shell settings list system | Select-String -Pattern 'emergency|cell_broadcast|cellbroadcast'

tasks.title: Any test or diagnostic Cell Broadcast component
tasks.reason: Phase 4's central hope: does Samsung ship a legitimate test-alert interface, as AOSP does? This looks for it in the package list and in the receiver package's component table. Finding nothing is a valid and useful result; we then know the phone has no built-in test entry point.
commands: adb shell pm list packages | Select-String -Pattern 'test|diagnostic|factory'
adb shell dumpsys package com.android.cellbroadcastreceiver | Select-String -Pattern 'Activity|test' -Context 4
adb shell dumpsys package com.samsung.android.cellbroadcastreceiver | Select-String -Pattern 'Activity|test' -Context 4
tasks.note: Do not launch anything found here yet. Discovery only in this batch.

tasks.title: What this adb session is and is not allowed to do
tasks.reason: Records the identity of the shell process on the phone (which UID adb runs as), because that is what determines what adb can and cannot reach. This is the fact behind 'adb is transport, not privilege escalation'.
tasks.note: The 'su -c id' line is expected to fail on a stock phone. Its failure IS the finding: it confirms no root shell is available. Do not attempt to install or obtain root.

tasks.title: Every receiver across the Cell Broadcast surface
tasks.reason: The previous tasks look at two guessed package names. A Samsung build can carry the receiver under a name neither guess covers, and can add OEM components that participate. This enumerates receivers from every package that could plausibly take part, so the report does not depend on guessing the package name correctly.
commands: adb shell dumpsys package com.android.cellbroadcastreceiver | Select-String -Pattern 'Receiver' -Context 0,12
adb shell dumpsys package com.samsung.android.cellbroadcastreceiver | Select-String -Pattern 'Receiver' -Context 0,12
adb shell dumpsys package com.google.android.cellbroadcastreceiver | Select-String -Pattern 'Receiver' -Context 0,12
adb shell dumpsys package com.samsung.android.emergency | Select-String -Pattern 'Receiver' -Context 0,12
adb shell pm list packages | Select-String -Pattern 'samsung'
adb shell pm list packages -f | Select-String -Pattern 'cellbroadcast'
tasks.note: If a package in this list does not exist, that absence is a finding, not an error to work around. Send the output as it appears.

tasks.title: AppOps, notification state and the local simulator's own permissions
tasks.reason: Android 14+ denies USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT by default for apps that are not calling or alarm apps, and a denied op silently degrades a full-screen alert into a heads-up notification. Separately, the repository recorded a false 'notification permission is not granted' reading for the local simulator app; this collects the raw evidence needed to tell a real denial from an unreadable probe.
commands: adb shell appops get com.tirodz.emergencysimulator USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT
tasks.note: If the app is not installed, the command will say so; send that. Do not install it for this batch.

tasks.title: Carrier configuration and which Cell Broadcast channels are enabled
tasks.reason: A correctly formed message on a channel that is disabled, or whose range is not marked displayable, is accepted and then discarded without any alert. This is the difference between 'the pipeline ran and produced no alert' and 'the alert UI was reached'. Without this, a silent result cannot be interpreted.
commands: adb shell settings list global | Select-String -Pattern 'cell_broadcast|emergency|alert'
adb shell settings list secure | Select-String -Pattern 'cell_broadcast|emergency|alert'
adb shell dumpsys activity services | Select-String -Pattern 'cellbroadcast|CellBroadcast' -Context 4,4
tasks.note: This is the task that most often explains a silent result. Send it whole.

tasks.title: The two gates that decide whether any test path exists
tasks.reason: Gate 1 and gate 3 from docs/stock-device/cell-broadcast-gate-model.md. ro.debuggable decides whether the AOSP test receiver is registered at all (Path 1), and the framework resource config_disable_all_cb_messages decides whether the platform drops every Cell Broadcast message before the handler sees it. Both are read-only reads of values the platform derives. ro.debuggable is also read by the paste's own device report, so this task corroborates it.
commands: adb shell cmd overlay list --user 0 | Select-String -Pattern 'cellbroadcast|telephony|framework'
adb shell cmd overlay dump | Select-String -Pattern 'disable_all_cb|cellbroadcast' -Context 2,2
adb shell dumpsys activity broadcasts | Select-String -Pattern 'protected' -Context 1,2
adb shell settings get global cell_broadcast_emergency_alerts

tasks.title: Whether the CellBroadcast app testing mode exists on this firmware
tasks.reason: Path 2 from the gate model. AOSP registers a dialer secret-code receiver for *#*#2627#*#* that toggles the app preference 'testing_mode'; the handler accepts it when ro.debuggable==1 OR the app resource allow_testing_mode_on_user_build is true (AOSP ships it true). If Samsung kept this, testing mode is reachable on a retail phone without a debug build. This task only DETECTS the receiver and reads the preference; it does not send the secret code and does not write the preference.
commands: adb shell dumpsys package com.android.cellbroadcastreceiver | Select-String -Pattern 'SECRET_CODE|2627|secret_code' -Context 3,3
adb shell dumpsys package com.samsung.android.cellbroadcastreceiver | Select-String -Pattern 'SECRET_CODE|2627|secret_code' -Context 3,3
adb shell pm list packages | Select-String -Pattern 'secret|dialer|phone'
adb shell dumpsys package com.android.cellbroadcastreceiver | Select-String -Pattern 'CellBroadcastReceiver' -Context 0,10
adb shell cmd appops get com.android.cellbroadcastreceiver

tasks.title: The carrier-side Cell Broadcast restriction and channel ranges
tasks.reason: Gate 4 and gate 5 from the gate model. CellBroadcastAlertService filters a message whose carrier channel range is marked test-mode-only unless the device is in testing mode, and drops messages on channels with no enabled range. This is the difference between 'the injection failed' and 'the injection worked and the platform discarded it', and only the carrier configuration can tell them apart.
commands: adb shell settings list global | Select-String -Pattern 'cell_broadcast'
adb shell settings list secure | Select-String -Pattern 'cell_broadcast'

after_this_batch: Return the raw outputs and stop there.

A follow-up batch will be authored based on what these show. If the receiver package exposes a legitimate, non-privileged test entry point, the next batch will attempt it (with explicit approval, and only if it does not modify the phone).
If no such entry point exists, the conclusion is the legitimate boundary: a stock A35 has no externally reachable test path, and we document that rather than working around it.
revision_note: Tasks 11-13 added after the first read-only pass was scoped. Tasks 1-10 establish identity and the two guessed Cell Broadcast package names; tasks 11-13 cover the components of any name, the AppOps/notification state, and the carrier configuration that decides whether a correctly delivered message becomes an alert. Tasks 14-16 were added after a full read of the AOSP sources this session (see docs/stock-device/cell-broadcast-gate-model.md). Tasks 1-13 find the components; 14-16 read the three gates that decide whether a component that exists is ever allowed to run. Every one of the three is invisible from a package list and from an exit code.
